title: Keep Every (Textable, Numeric)
description: Stride for sequence decimation: keep one item out of every N
documentation:
## Purpose
Stride parameter for the [Decimate Sequence](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:decimate-sequence;in=media:;out=media:) cap. The decimator keeps items at positions `0, N, 2N, …` of the input sequence and drops the rest.

## When to use
Use to subsample a long sequence — every Nth frame from a video disbinder, every Nth record from a CSV, every Nth file from a folder. With `N = 1` (or no value), the sequence passes through unchanged.

## Notes
Must be a positive integer. Negative, zero, or non-integer values fail loudly rather than being silently treated as 1, so a misspelled flag does not silently disable decimation.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Numeric
Coercion marker indicating the value supports numeric operations (addition,
comparison, ordering). Independent of `textable`; a numeric value is often
also textable (an integer is encodable as text), but neither implies the
other in general.

The value supports numeric operations.
